Hello and good morning! **Mehdi** here. Thank goodness it's Friday, _amirite_?
Although, having said that, ending _this_ week means we're starting _next_
week, and next week… is _MIDTERMS_ week. American democracy, no exaggeration,
is on the line. Yes, again. (**FYI:** I'll be live in Michigan with **Zeteo
's** **Prem Thakker** on Tuesday night, so do join our livestream on Substack
and [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@zeteo/streams) then.)

In today's **' First Draft,'** it's time to thank the Clintons (yes, the
_Clintons_!) for doing what many centrist Democrats refuse to do ahead of
these midterms. And it's also sadly time to mourn the loss of one of the great
actors of our time, the one and only **Sir Patrick Stewart** aka Captain Jean-
Luc Picard aka Professor Charles Xavier.

Let's get into it - oh, and no paywall on today's 'First Draft,' so do share
with your friends and colleagues and get them to sign up too.

## **Even the Clintons Get It - So Why Can't the Rest of the Centrists?**

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!L0Yb!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-
post-
media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F88fb5968-6337-4abb-8527-3470d38e741d_1024x780.jpeg)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!L0Yb!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-
post-
media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F88fb5968-6337-4abb-8527-3470d38e741d_1024x780.jpeg)_Hillary
Clinton and Bill Clinton attend a ceremony to commemorate the 25th anniversary
of 9/11, in New York City. Photo: Barry Williams/Pool/Getty Images._

I've never been a fan of the Clintons.

Bill's triangulating presidency dragged the Democratic Party to the right on
everything from welfare to crime to foreign policy. Hillary backed the
disastrous Iraq and Libya wars and then lost to Donald Trump.

In recent years, they've both been ardent advocates for Israel, too.

Remember Bill going to Michigan - Michigan, of all places, home to one of the
largest Arab-American populations - in the final days of the 2024 presidential
campaign, to [tell](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/10/31/bill-clinton-
criticised-for-saying-israel-forced-to-kill-gaza-civilians) voters that
Israelis **" were there first"** in Palestine and that the Israeli military
had been **" forced"** to kill Palestinian civilians?

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

Remember Hillary [repeatedly](https://www.nytimes.com/2024/05/09/us/hillary-
clinton-morning-joe-israel-history.html)
[lecturing](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/oqdQx8F-jec) pro-Palestinian
protesters about their supposed ignorance of Middle Eastern history and
accusing them of being brainwashed by TikTok?

Yes, those Clintons.

But credit where credit is due.

Because in recent days, as Republicans have escalated their vile, racist, and
Islamophobic attacks on Abdul El-Sayed, the Muslim and Arab-American
Democratic Senate candidate in the crucial swing state of Michigan, and as a
depressing number of centrist Democrats have either looked the other way or
actively joined the pile-on, two unlikely voices have spoken up.

Bill Clinton. And Hillary Clinton.

Yes, really.

In South Florida the other day, the former president delivered an impassioned
defense of Islam and Muslims, condemning the Republicans' relentless attempts
to divide Americans along religious lines:

> **" I'm tired of people denigrating Muslims for being Muslims.**
>
> **" The Koran says, and I first heard this from my daughter, who read the
> Koran from start to finish when she was 15 years old, and she said, 'Dad,
> read this.'**
>
> **" 'Allah put the different people on the earth not that they might despise
> one another, but that they might come to know one another and learn from one
> another.'**
>
> **" There are bad actors in every faith because we're all flawed human
> beings.**
>
> **" But the religious wars, the culture wars, I'm just tired."**

On this week's episode of 'High Stakes,' Hillary Clinton's new podcast with
journalist Kara Swisher, the former secretary of state and Democratic
presidential nominee took aim at the GOP's anti-Muslim fearmongering against
El-Sayed. Republicans, she argued, are trying to get Americans to **" not vote
their interests, but vote their fears":**

> **"[Mike Rogers'] surrogates and a lot of the independent expenditure media
> is really fearmongering against El-Sayed as a Muslim, trying to link him to
> the Muslim Brotherhood, and all of that… I'm just tired of that, and I hope
> people are tired of that. Judge somebody on who they are, what they stand
> for, what they produce… This is not about woke, this is about broke. If you
> can't win on affordability, if you are bankrupting the country and enriching
> yourself personally, try to divert attention."**

Now, I never thought I would find myself saying this, but Bill and Hillary
Clinton are right.

They're right to call out the bigotry. They're right to condemn the
fearmongering. They're right to stand up to the Republicans' cynical attempt
to weaponize a Muslim candidate's faith.

The Clintons say they are **" tired" **of the GOP's relentless and cynical
anti-Muslim bigotry.

But my question is: Why aren't the rest of the centrist Democrats? Where is
their outrage?

Why did Rep. Haley Stevens, who was defeated by El-Sayed in the Michigan
primary in August, go on CNN on Wednesday night and
[lambast](https://x.com/kaitlancollins/status/2115622786680951244) her fellow
Democrat over an ad he had nothing to do with while saying not one word about
the racist attacks he has had to endure from the right? Why is her fiance
[proudly
voting](https://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/politics/2026/10/28/haley-
stevens-fiance-jason-turkish-voting-for-mike-rogers-abdul-el-sayed-israel-
jewish/92480200007/?gnt-cfr=1&gca-cat=p&gca-uir=true&gca-
epti=z114830p119150l000050c119150e115175v114830d--xx--b--xx--&gca-ft=39&gca-
ds=sophi) for Republican Mike Rogers, who has
[agreed](https://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/politics/2026/10/10/barstool-
founder-dave-portnoy-calls-abdul-el-sayed-a-terrorist-rogers-
agrees/92190617007/?gnt-cfr=1&gca-cat=p&gca-uir=true&gca-
epti=z113330p117150l000550c117150e110575v113330d--52--b--52--&gca-ft=148&gca-
ds=sophi) with people who call El-Sayed a **" terrorist" **and whose own
[faith adviser](https://rogersforsenate.com/news/rogers-announces-faith-
coalition-leadership-team) has
[called](https://www.cbsnews.com/detroit/news/dearborn-city-council-meeting-
changes-location-christian-crusader-march/) Islam a **" death cult"**?

Why is Rep. Josh Gottheimer, one of Israel's most strident defenders in
Congress, indulging GOP smears against El-Sayed and
[telling](https://x.com/wallyrashid/status/2115189619574657295) interviewers,
**" There's no way I am ever coming out for El-Sayed right now"**?

Why did Senator John Fetterman falsely
[accuse](https://www.abc27.com/national/fetterman-dubs-el-sayed-pontiac-
platner-in-response-to-ogre-on-a-pike-quip/) El-Sayed of being **" pro-
Hamas"**?

Why can't Nancy Pelosi bring herself to even say El-Sayed's name,
[referring](https://www.wfmd.com/2026/10/29/nancy-pelosi-calls-mamdani-el-
sayeds-past-comments-on-israel-concerning-and-wrong/) to him only as **" this
new person in Michigan"**?

Meanwhile, there is deafening silence from the top of the Democratic Party.
Where on earth is Senator Chuck Schumer? Has anyone heard from him recently?
Has the man who wants to be Senate majority leader again issued any statements
or given any interviews denouncing the bigoted attacks on the Muslim
Democratic Senate candidate in must-win Michigan? How about Senator Kirsten
Gillibrand, chair of the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee? Then again,
Gillibrand has been no stranger to Islamophobic fearmongering herself,
infamously [referring](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/jul/02/zohran-
mamdani-kirsten-gillibrand-apologizes) to Zohran Mamdani, the Muslim
Democratic mayor of New York, as a supporter of **" global jihad."** As for
Schumer, he
[handpicked](https://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/politics/2026/06/17/chuck-
schumer-endorsement-haley-stevens-abdul-el-sayed-mallory-
mcmorrow/90591653007/?gnt-cfr=1&gca-cat=p&gca-uir=true&gca-
epti=z113530p119050l001250c119050e007675v113530d--34--b--34--&gca-ft=180&gca-
ds=sophi) Haley Stevens as his candidate in the Michigan Senate Democratic
primary.

The bigotry from right-wing Republicans is off the charts. It's disgusting,
but it isn't surprising.

What's surprising, _shocking_ even, is how many supposedly liberal, supposedly
tolerant, supposedly anti-racist centrist Democrats seem utterly unbothered by
that bigotry when its target happens to be a Muslim. Some remain silent.
Others join in.

I would go so far as to argue that Republicans get away with their vicious
racism and bigotry because so many centrist Democrats - with the thankful and
notable exception of the Clintons this week! - go along with it. The same
centrist Democrats who proudly profess to be _against_ racism and bigotry when
the targets of it _aren 't_ Muslims.

As John Stuart Mill famously
[observed](https://www.goodreads.com/quotes/17188-bad-men-need-nothing-more-
to-compass-their-ends-than): **" Bad men need nothing more to compass their
ends, than that good men should look on and do nothing."**

But in this case, many centrist Democrats aren't merely looking on and doing
nothing. They're actively making the bad men's jobs easier.

## Rest in Power, Captain Picard 😢

I'm not sure I've ever shared this publicly, but I'm a bit of a Trekkie, so
[Patrick
Stewart's](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/29/arts/television/patrick-stewart-
dead.html?smid=nytcore-ios-share) death at the age of 86 on Wednesday hit me
pretty hard.

Growing up, I loved watching 'Star Trek: The Next Generation,' which aired in
the late 1980s and early 1990s and starred Stewart as Jean-Luc Picard, the
second-most famous, but undeniably the best, captain of the USS Enterprise.

Watching Stewart, a Shakespearean stage actor with a ["commanding baritone
voice,"](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/29/arts/television/patrick-stewart-
dead.html?smid=nytcore-ios-share) deliver rousing monologues as Picard gave me
chills. The clip above, from the 1996 movie 'Star Trek: First Contact,' is one
of my favorite scenes involving Stewart.

Stewart passed away from Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia just 51
days before the U.S. release of 'Avengers: Doomsday,' in which the award-
winning British actor reprised his _other_ famous Hollywood sci-fi role as
Professor Charles Xavier, leader of the X-Men. Stewart played Xavier, aka
Professor X, in six 'X-Men' movies between 2000 and 2014.

I admired him not just for his acting, but for his politics too: He was a
[loud critic](https://ktla.com/news/nationworld/british-actor-patrick-stewart-
applies-for-u-s-citizenship-to-fight-trump-presidency/) of Donald Trump, an
[opponent](https://www.theguardian.com/culture/2020/jan/15/sir-patrick-
stewart-speaks-of-brexit-sorrow-at-star-trek-launch) of Brexit, a
[supporter](https://x.com/SirPatStew/status/243818555945123840) of the
Palestinians, and a [lifelong
socialist](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/theatre/drama/7598529/Patrick-
Stewart-interview.html).

In 2003, in an
[interview](https://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/profiles/patrick-
stewart-the-spirit-of-enterprise-111029.html) with _The Independent_ , Stewart
said some of his fellow British actors thought he was "slumming it" for
agreeing to play characters in Hollywood sci-fi shows and movies.

"What crap! What snobbery!" he said. "For huge numbers of people, I will
always be Jean-Luc Picard, and that's fine."

Indeed. Rest in power, Jean-Luc, _rest in power._

**[ICE Is Running One of the Largest Anti-Left Surveillance Operations in US
History.](https://www.wired.com/story/ice-is-running-one-of-the-largest-anti-

facing federal conspiracy charges" arising from opposing ICE operations

unconstitutional spying operation carried out by Immigration and Customs
Enforcement against left-wing social movements in Minnesota and beyond."
Describing a DHS weaponized against dissent, Winston writes: "Nothing of this

counterinsurgency against the New Left and the anti-war movement in the 1960s
and 1970s."

**[Mike Rogers's Wife Runs a Consultancy That Sells Government
Access.](https://prospect.org/2026/10/29/mike-rogerss-wife-runs-a-consultancy-
that-sells-government-access/)**

Admittedly, this piece from the _American Prospect_ has a headline akin to
"Dog Bites Man" and "Water Wet," given its subject, Kristi Rogers, is married
to one of the swampiest Swamp creatures of all, Republican congressman turned
GOP Michigan Senate candidate Mike Rogers. It's worth reading, as Rogers' race
with Democrat Abdul El-Sayed goes right down to the wire. "Ms. Rogers runs a
Beltway trade group representing energy traders, mining companies, and
manufacturers in their efforts to influence federal officials and federal
policy," Zachary Groz writes. "According to ethics watchdogs, Ms. Rogers's
position, which has not been previously reported, raises the potential for
serious conflicts of interest should her husband win."

**[Hospital beds for the nation's sickest kids are
disappearing.](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/pediatric-intensive-care-units-
closing-nationwide/)**

For KFF Health News and CBS, Katheryn Houghton provides a devastating account
of the appalling state of children's healthcare under the Trump administration
and a GOP Congress, a problem particularly acute for rural areas more likely
to vote Republican. "Depending on the hospital," Houghton writes, from
Montana, "pediatric units - which are separate from neonatal intensive care
units - can serve patients ranging from a few weeks old to well into their
teens or early adulthood. As hospitals look to cut costs, many are converting
those beds into more services for newborns or adults. As a result, pediatric
intensive care has become centralized in medical hubs, requiring critically
ill children to travel farther for lifesaving care."
